title: Currier page 59’s historical grouping survives length and leaf checks, with only five joint modern sides at 375 glyphs
statement: The Petersen-number crosswalk maps all 40 entries in D'Imperio's Figure 6, including historical p59 to f31r and the 12 Biological B sides to six whole leaves. Using the archived Currier transcript, f31r is closest on average to Biological B in first windows of 350, 375, or 400 readable glyphs. With the first up to 400 glyphs of all 40 sides and siblings kept in one physical block, f31r has correlation distance 0.078663 to Biological B and 0.123918 to Herbal B. The normalized Manhattan distances are 0.346667 and 0.414986. Removing any one of the 25 other physical leaves preserves both rankings. Two disjoint 200-glyph windows on the same 31 sides both preserve the ranking. The modern open practice panel has six usable paired sides at 350 EVA-basic units and five at 375 and 400, with no f31r. At 375 the single independent Biological B leaf-pair has correlation distance 0.053412 in ZL and 0.056872 in IT. The corresponding medians against Herbal B are 0.089805 and 0.110149 across two leaf-pairs. Only three Biological B sides from two leaves supply the later matched windows. Across the broader Currier B practice selection, Hand 2 has two Biological leaves and one Herbal leaf, and Hand 5 has only Herbal leaves. This supports the historical nearest-group contrast using alternative distance summaries. The modern paired sample is insufficient to reproduce the placement of f31r or separate section from hand.
check: Before interpreting a section effect, report the count of complete independent physical leaves crossing hand and section, with both transliterations aligned at shared paragraph loci. If coverage permits, repeat the same two distances within Currier B and hand on matched text lengths and folio or quire blocks. Compare first and later windows within that matched sample. A direct f31r replication requires an independently documented contemporary transcription of that folio in the comparison sample.

historical_report.document: NSA DOCID 6588666, June 1978, printed Figure 6 on p. 18 (PDF page 27).

page_crosswalk.method: Transcribed the five separated blocks of Figure 6 in order (12 Biological B, 7 Herbal A, 4 Herbal B, 9 Herbal A, 8 Herbal B). Joined the old page number to the unique Petersen-number row in IVTFF Annex 1 marked Y. Checked Currier Table A and the historical/IVTFF line texts for p59 and p147.

analysis: Preserve historical alphanumeric glyphs in page-line order and omit spaces, editorial markers and unresolved glyphs. All 40 historical sides are present. Pages 68, 72 and 110 have only 312, 308 and 346 recorded glyphs. The original windows were approximate and their precise endpoints are unavailable. The complete panel therefore uses a 400-glyph cap and retains shorter sides at their recorded length.

For each page count symbols, normalize by the number of symbols selected, and use correlation distance 1 minus Pearson r and the Manhattan distance. Use a single pooled alphabet over the historical panel and a joint pooled alphabet across ZL and IT within each modern comparison. These are descriptive distances in the spirit of the original study. Its five clustering or scaling algorithms are outside this replay.

For within-group and between-group results first average all eligible side pairs for each distinct physical-leaf pair, then take the median across those pairs. For the named f31r example average side distances within each other physical leaf and then over leaves in a group. Exclude f31v and every same-leaf comparison.

Use only the site's open public practice evaluation subset for modern ZL and IT. Match paragraph locus IDs and verify that the first locus and common order agree. Form windows on the common sequence, counting known glyphs and keeping common starts. Later windows begin with the first common paragraph line after both versions have already reached the first window width. Retain only complete windows in both versions. The parallel raw-EVA result tests segmentation sensitivity.

For broader within-hand support, examine all Currier B practice leaves with the necessary aligned windows and count distinct physical leaves per section under ZL's published hand attribution. Both sections need at least two leaves before a within-hand distance contrast is reported. No significance calculation is used.

reproduction.instructions: In a checkout at the listed project commit with its pinned inputs fetched, copy the embedded compare.py and historical.py strings into a work directory. Write panel as panel.json in that directory. Download the historical archive as original-currier.txt. From the project root run PYTHONPATH=. python3 /path/to/compare.py /path/to/original-currier.txt /path/to/result.json.
reproduction.historical.py:
"""Extract glyph streams from the archived Currier–D'Imperio voynich.orig.

Each card row starts with the old three-digit page number, two-digit line
number and Currier A/B label. This archive has no separate page headings.
The rows are already in physical page and line order. Pages omitted by the
archive stay omitted, and a duplicate or out-of-order record is an error.

The witness uses one uppercase letter or digit per transcribed glyph. Digits
in the body remain glyphs, including rare 0 and 5, which the Currier alphabet
documents explicitly. The header digits, / word spaces, line-end hyphens and
# paragraph ends contribute no glyphs. The parallel IVTFF edition aligns
internal hyphens to breaks in the written line around illustrations, and * and
comma to unreadable glyphs. The three uncertain raw $ and _ entries also
contribute no glyphs. Their later IVTFF readings (2, R and O) are editorial
choices and are kept out of this archival extraction.
"""

import re
from pathlib import Path


_RECORD = re.compile(r"([0-9]{3})([0-9]{2})[AB] +([A-Z0-9/\-#*,_$]+)")
_GLYPH = re.compile(r"[A-Z0-9]")


def historical_pages(path: str | Path) -> dict[int, list[str]]:
    """Return the known single glyphs of each old page in archive line order."""
    archive = Path(path)
    pages = {}
    previous = (0, 0)
    with archive.open(encoding="ascii") as source:
        for row_number, line in enumerate(source, 1):
            line = line.rstrip("\n")
            if not line:
                continue
            record = _RECORD.fullmatch(line)
            if record is None:
                raise ValueError(f"{archive}:{row_number}: unrecognized Currier record")
            page, number = map(int, record.groups()[:2])
            if (page, number) <= previous:
                raise ValueError(f"{archive}:{row_number}: duplicate or out-of-order page/line")
            previous = page, number
            pages.setdefault(page, []).extend(_GLYPH.findall(record[3]))
    return pages

independent_historical_audit.method: Separate calculation with statistics.correlation and the 34 glyphs observed in the capped 400-glyph panel. Side distances were averaged by physical leaf. Both non-overlapping 200-glyph windows used the same 31-side ≥400 subset.
